title: Context slab format and merge heuristics (sketch)
content:
Purpose:

This is a working sketch for a compact client/server context artifact I'm calling a 'Context Slab' and a set of merge/eviction heuristics for stitching slabs into a coherent prompt window. Goal: give client-side prefetch + progressive hydration a compact, auditable, and mergeable on-disk/network format that can be reconciled deterministically by the runtime.

Design constraints / goals:
- Compact serialized blobs (suitable for mobile/edge caches).
- Mergeable without full re-tokenization when possible (use token-range + anchoring metadata).
- Deterministic tie-breaks for concurrent sources (local slab, remote slab, ephemeral tool output).
- Provenance + lightweight checksums for forensic replay and telemetry.
- Allow partial hydration (payloads can be lazy-fetched).

High-level concept:
- A Slab represents a contiguous set of contextual items anchored to token ranges: system instructions, user messages, assistant messages, tool outputs, and embeddings references.
- Each item has stable ids, a token-length estimate, a compact checksum, and an optional external reference (URL/id) for large payloads.
- Merge is a 3-phase algorithm: reconcile spans, prefer higher-priority authoritative sources, collapse duplicates, and compact to meet a target token budget.

On-disk / wire shape (informal pseudo-spec):

ContextSlab {
  slab_id: string (GUID),
  sequence: int (monotonic slab generation),
  anchors: [ { anchor_id: string, token_start: int, token_end: int } ],
  items: [ item_id1, item_id2, ... ] (ordered by token position),
  priority: string (local|remote|ephemeral|archive),
  ttl_seconds: int,
  created_at: ISO8601,
  checksum: base64(short),
  metadata: { free-form tags } (optional),
  compact_index: base64(binary index for quick lookup),
  // payloads may be embedded or referenced externally
  payloads: [ { item_id: string, compressed_payload_b64?: string, external_ref?: string, size_bytes: int } ]
}

Item (semantic unit) fields (represented inline in payloads or as separate entries):
- item_id: stable id (sha1-like short)
- item_type: system|user|assistant|tool|embed-ref
- provenance: source-id (client|server|tool/<id>)
- token_estimate: int
- created_at: ISO8601
- checksum: base64(short)
- content_hint: short human label ("last-user-msg", "summary-anch", etc)

Merge heuristics (sketch):
Inputs: target_budget_tokens, candidate_slabs (ordered newest-first), local_context (optional)
1) Preselect slabs whose ttl not expired and checksum != null.
2) Build a token map by item token ranges (token_estimate + token_start). When two items overlap:
   a) If identical checksum -> dedupe and prefer item from higher-priority slab.
   b) If different checksum -> compare provenance priority map: local > remote > archive by default; ephemeral wins only if marked high-priority.
   c) If provenance ties, use sequence higher (newer) first, then slab_id lexical tie-break.
3) Collapse adjacent assistant/user items if they are of same type and there is no intervening tool output; merge by concatenation and set merged checksum = hash(a+b).
4) If after dedupe the total token_estimate > target_budget_tokens:
   - Strategy A (preserve recency): drop earliest archive slabs first, then remote, then local oldest; shrink items with 'compress_hint' (summaries) where available; finally, apply lossy summarization hook (external call).
   - Strategy B (preserve system/instruction): ensure system messages and tool outputs are atomic; they are not trimmed unless explicitly allowed.
5) Produce a merged slab manifest with mapping from original item_ids to merged positions (for debug/replay).
6) Validation: compute merged checksum; if client has partial payloads referenced externally, return a 'missing_payloads' list for lazy fetch.

API sketch (HTTP):
POST /v1/context/merge
Request JSON:
{
  "slab_candidates": ["slab_id1", "slab_id2"],
  "client_manifest": { "known_checksums": ["c1","c2"], "local_priority_overrides": {"slab_idX":"force"} },
  "target_budget_tokens": 1024,
  "merge_strategy": "preserve_recency"
}
Response JSON:
{
  "merged_slab_id": "guid",
  "items": [ { "item_id":"...", "token_start": 0, "token_end": 56, "origin_slabs": ["slabA"] } ],
  "missing_payloads": [ "item_id3" ],
  "final_checksum": "base64...",
  "debug_map": [ "orig_item->merged_pos" ]
}

Notes on partial hydration / lazy fetch:
- Payloads may be "placeholder" entries with small metadata and external_ref pointing to a fetchable blob. When merge determines a placeholder is required, it is returned in merged manifest and client will fetch in background.
- Keep a small priority queue on client for fetching missing_payloads ordered by merged position and user-visible scores (near-cursor items first).

Telemetry & auditability
- Emit slab life-cycle events: slab_created, slab_merged_request, slab_merged_result (include slab_ids, token_totals, shrink_actions).
- Keep a short map of checksums -> human hints for offline evaluation of quality regressions.

Open questions / TODOs:
- token_estimate accuracy: use model-tokenizer v2 approximations; capture variance range so merges can be conservative.
- How to express semantic equivalence beyond checksum? (fuzzy-lc fingerprinting?)
- Controlled summarization hook: where does it run (client or server)? cost model?
- Garbage collection: how long to keep archive slabs vs local? Need policy by tenant and platform.
- Security: external_ref fetches must honor tenant-scoped auth; consider signed URLs with short TTL.

Implementation notes / low-friction prototype plan:
- Start with a single-file slab protoschema (JSON) + small JS merge function that operates on token_estimates and checksums.
- Add a CLI tool to replay merges from telemetry logs and visualize diffs.
- Hook up to the existing ingestion pipeline as optional "slab export" for new session checkpoints.

Quick ascii sketch (merge flow):

[local slab V5]   [remote slab V8]   [archive slab V3]
     |                 |                  |
     v                 v                  v
  item map ------> dedupe/collate --------> sort by priority
                                      |
                                      v
                           budget trim / summarization
                                      |
                                      v
                               merged slab manifest

------
Notes to self: commit a minimal prototype under gh-rl/infer-runtime/tmp/context-slab-proto and add a small test that demonstrates deterministic tie-breaks when two slabs include a different assistant summary of the same user turn.

End of sketch. Will iterate after Ben/Ruth feedback.
